page: OVHcloud b3-8 is an entry-level general purpose virtual server configured with 2 dedicated AMD EPYC physical cores running at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. Operating on a KVM hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, each core features a 1:1 thread mapping with no multithreading enabled. The CPU cache layout provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by instruction flags including AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI, while excluding modern vector instruction sets like AVX-512 or AMX.

The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled directly via an integrated 50 GB NVMe SSD, but the instance does not feature dedicated graphics processing hardware, providing a GPU count of zero. Network connectivity exhibits a baseline bandwidth rate of 0 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned to the instance.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng tests, alongside average outcomes in single-core Geekbench metrics, large-block memory read/write operations, and single-threaded gzip compression. However, overall multi-core performance remains limited due to the 2-vCPU hardware footprint, producing low relative scores in PassMark CPU tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and code compilation suites. Static web serving throughput ranks in the lower percentiles, and LLM inference is limited to light text generation using sub-billion-parameter models.

OVHcloud b3-8 delivers steady baseline compute efficiency through dedicated x86_64 cores and high-speed NVMe storage. Because parallel processing capacity is inherently constrained by its two cores and low baseline networking profile, the instance is primarily suited for lightweight backend services, small web servers, basic CI/CD runners, and development or testing environments.

The server runs under a KVM hypervisor with a single thread per core and does not include GPU acceleration. It delivers strong single-core stress-ng performance and moderate single-threaded decompression rates, though overall throughput in multi-core metrics, PassMark scoring, and compilation tasks reflects the constraints of its two-core setup. With a balanced 4.0 GB memory-to-core ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, OVHcloud b3-8 serves lightweight production environments, small application backends, dev/test setups, and entry-level database tasks requiring steady CPU availability.
